subject: Startups
title: Liquidation Preferences
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Liquidation Preferences.

hook.text: Your startup sells for $50M. You think you'll get $25M for your 50% stake. Then liquidation preferences kick in.

buildup.text: Liquidation preferences determine who gets paid first when a company is sold.

discovery.text: A 1x non-participating preference means investors get their investment back, then the rest is split. Standard and fair.

twist.text: Participating preferred is brutal: investors get their money back AND share in the remaining proceeds.

climax.text: In a modest exit, liquidation preferences can leave founders with almost nothing. The headline price is not your payout.

punchline.text: The exit price is not your check. Read the preferences.

quiz.question: What does a 1x liquidation preference mean?
options: Investors get double their money first
Investors get their investment back before others
